draft.title: Ways of describing mental wellbeing
card: Mental wellbeing is not just the absence of a mental health problem. It can be described in more than one way.
Functioning
how well a person manages daily life, such as study, work, relationships and looking after themselves. High functioning means they can do these things well.
Resilience
the ability to cope with and adapt to stress, change or hard times, and then carry on. A resilient person can recover from setbacks.
Social and emotional wellbeing
how a person feels and how well they connect with others. It covers handling emotions and having positive relationships.
draft.remember: High wellbeing can show up as strong functioning, resilience, and good social and emotional wellbeing.

a.q: Which description best shows high resilience in a student?
opts: Returns to study after failing a test and adjusts her plan
Never feels upset about anything that happens at school
Avoids hard subjects so that she does not feel stressed
Completes every task on time without any effort at all
a.why: Resilience is coping with a setback and adapting, so she recovers and carries on. Completing tasks on time without effort is closer to functioning, and it does not involve facing a hard time.
a.clue: Look for coping with a setback and carrying on.

b.q: Arjun has lost his job. He still cooks, pays his bills and attends training each week. Which feature of mental wellbeing does this most directly show?
opts: High functioning, as he keeps managing daily life
High resilience, as he has recovered from the job loss
Good emotional wellbeing, as he feels happy about it
Strong social wellbeing, as he has many close friends
b.why: The scenario describes how well he manages daily tasks, which is functioning. It does not say he has recovered, how he feels, or anything about his relationships, so the other options claim more than the scenario shows.
b.clue: Focus on what he actually does each day.

a.best: Returns to study after failing a test and adjusts her plan

b.best: High functioning, as he keeps managing daily life
also_right: High resilience, as he has recovered from the job loss

problems.detail: The card defines social and emotional wellbeing generically as how a person feels and connects with others. The VCE Study Design and point 3 treat SEWB as a multidimensional, holistic view of wellbeing as both an individual and collective experience, illustrated by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander conceptions (body, mind, family, community, culture, Country, spirituality). This narrower definition clashes with point 3.

SEWB has its own point (point 3). This card defines it in its own terms instead of only naming it as one of the ways of describing mental wellbeing. That risks teaching a definition that point 3 then replaces.

Carrying on with cooking, bills and training after losing a job fits the card's own definition of resilience: coping with hard times and then carrying on. So the resilience option is defensible. Only the added words 'has recovered' and 'most directly' separate it from functioning, which may confuse careful students.

check.summary: The card's generic definition of social and emotional wellbeing conflicts with the VCE holistic SEWB framework taught in point 3. Question b's resilience option is also defensible from the card's own definition of resilience.

flags: Question b: the checker says “High resilience, as he has recovered from the job loss” could also be right.

proposal.title: Ways of describing mental wellbeing
card: Mental wellbeing is more than the absence of a mental health disorder. It can be shown in more than one way.
Functioning
how well a person manages daily life, such as study, work, relationships and self-care. High functioning means they do these things well, day to day.
Resilience
the ability to cope with and adapt to stress or setbacks, then return to normal or better. It shows in how a person recovers over time, even if they struggle at first.
Social and emotional wellbeing
a third way, which takes a holistic view of wellbeing. It draws on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander understandings of wellbeing.
proposal.remember: High wellbeing can show in daily functioning, in bouncing back from setbacks, and in social and emotional wellbeing.

a.q: Which of these best shows high functioning in a student?
opts: Keeps up with study, work and self-care each week
Bounces back quickly each time she fails an exam
Never feels any stress, even during exam weeks
Has never been diagnosed with a mental health disorder
a.why: Functioning is how well a person manages daily life, such as study, work and self-care. Bouncing back after failing is resilience, which is about recovering from setbacks, not managing everyday tasks.
a.clue: Think about managing ordinary daily tasks.

b.q: After his family moved interstate, Tom struggled for a few weeks. He then joined a new club, changed his study routine and settled in. What does this show?
opts: High resilience, as he adapted and settled after the move
High functioning, as he managed daily life well throughout
Low wellbeing, as he struggled in the first few weeks
Low resilience, as he was upset by the move at first
b.why: Tom faced a setback, adapted and recovered over time, which is resilience. High functioning throughout is wrong, because he struggled to manage at first. Struggling early does not mean low resilience, since resilience shows in how a person recovers.
b.clue: Look at what happened after the hard first weeks.
